title: The Frobenius square of a k_0-morphism is Cartesian
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and put
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q=\varphi_q^{-1}\in\operatorname{Aut}(k/k_0)$, the
geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a
morphism of $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base], put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $f=f_0\times\operatorname{id}_k:X\to Y$,
where fibre products are as in [def-pc-fibre-product] and spectra and their induced morphisms as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let

$$
 g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):X\to X,\qquad
 g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):Y\to Y .
$$

Then:

1. $g_X$ and $g_Y$ are isomorphisms of schemes, with inverses
$\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma^{-1})$ and
$\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma^{-1})$;

2. $f\circ g_X=g_Y\circ f$;

3. the commutative square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
 X & \xrightarrow{\ g_X\ } & X\\
 f\downarrow & & \downarrow f\\
 Y & \xrightarrow{\ g_Y\ } & Y
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian: the morphism $(g_X,f):X\to X\times_{f,Y,g_Y}Y$ is an
isomorphism. This square, with the identification $(g_X,f)$, is the
*Frobenius square* of $f_0$.

In particular, for $Y_0=\Spec k_0$ one has $Y=s=\Spec k$ (via
$\Spec k_0\times_{k_0}k=\Spec k$), $g_Y=g_s=\Spec(\gamma)$, and for a
$k_0$-scheme $X_0$ with structure morphism $a_{X_0}$ the base change
$a_X:X\to s$ satisfies $a_X\circ g_X=g_s\circ a_X$, the square
$(a_X,g_X,g_s)$ being Cartesian.

source.place: Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, (1.1.10)(i) and (1.1.11), pp. 151-152: the action of W(F/F_q) on X = X_0 (x) F through the factor F, id_{X_0} x F being 'l'action du Frobenius geometrique' of (1.1.14), p. 152; the Cartesian property is the one asserted without proof in the slopmaster2 definition def:weil-direct-image-object (literature/blueprint/slopmaster2/src/version/sketch/01_final_weil_conjectures.tex, lines 2405-2425: 'The Frobenius square for f_0 is Cartesian') and in def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius

proof.text: Specialize the existing galoisMap_inverse theorem of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] to geometricFrobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic for the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], separately for X_0.hom and Y_0.hom. Its two components give the four displayed inverse identities, with precisely the prescribed inverse coefficient actions.

Bundle each coefficient action together with its explicit inverse and the identities from step 1 into an isomorphism of schemes. The IsIso instances of their hom morphisms give invertibility of the two horizontal maps. No finite-type hypothesis is needed.

For f=((Over.pullback b).map f_0).left, where b=Spec(algebraMap k_0 k), use pullback.hom_ext from [def-pc-fibre-product] to prove g_X followed by f equals f followed by g_Y. Over.pullback_map_left identifies f with the universal lift, so pullback.lift_fst and pullback.lift_snd compute its projections. Apply galoisMap_projections from [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] to both models. The first composites are both the first projection followed by f_0.left, and the second are both the second projection followed by Spec(gamma). The Over morphism [def-weil-scheme-over-base] supplies the compatibility in the universal lift.

Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_horiz_isIso to the commutative square from step 3 with the two isomorphism instances from step 2. This is the general universal-property argument giving the inverse r followed by g_X inverse to the canonical comparison (g_X,f) into the chosen pullback, so it proves exactly the required Cartesian square.

The second projection of the pullback of the identity structure morphism is an isomorphism by the standard pullback instance. For the structure square, unfold galoisMap to baseChangeMap along the Over endomorphism with left morphism Spec(gamma), as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Apply the existing AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_baseChangeMap theorem: its top map, vertical second projections and bottom Spec(gamma) are definitionally the displayed maps. This theorem proves the base-change square by pullback pasting, with no additional Frobenius-specific assumption.
